answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity through a slow reputation terrace: new agents start on a low, violet-tagged trust tier with tiny spending caps and must earn their way up by completing verified work over weeks, so spawning a thousand fresh identities buys nothing. A shale layer of stake helps too — each agent locks a deposit that is slashed if peers catch it attesting its own sock puppets, making fake volume cost more than it earns. Sybils are cheap to create but expensive to age, so time plus collateral is the filter.
